correctness.rationale: For n≥3, the claimed maximum and equality cases follow by run compositions. A balanced profile sums the two endpoint orientations, giving N/t times the binomial product in (1); an unbalanced profile has one forced orientation and product (2). At fixed t the centered loop split maximizes the product, strictly up to exchange for t≥2. For the unbalanced optimum, take a mode t≤r/2 and compare to the feasible balanced profile with t'=t+1 and (q',r')=(q+1,r). The comparison is strict except for the length-five equality in this intermediate bound, where the balanced global maximum is still larger. The centered balanced mode follows from the sign of AB−(A+B+3)k−2, with the single adjacent tie at n≡2 mod 4. Stirling at the centers up to bounded shifts gives the stated constant. At n=1 there is one empty spectrum and two words; at n=2 each spectrum is a singleton. Here the balanced-maximizer sentence is read in the n≥3 paragraph, not as saying the two transitions agree in all four singleton profiles at n=2. Independent literal enumeration of all 262,142 words of lengths 1–17 agrees with the maxima and n≥7 profiles; the frozen program was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The phrase ‘have the same counts’ means c01=c10 within each maximizing profile for n≥3, not that all maximizers share a common value of t.
